boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Trevilian Station record (June 11-12, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. The June 7–10 march, the June 20–21 White House fight and Saint Mary's Church (VA066, June 24) are the same raid but not this record. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions and the live field zero. NPS names Gregg's and Torbert's divisions against Hampton's and Fitzhugh Lee's. Hampton says he took Lee's division in addition to his own and cites a disparity in numbers. Sheridan's June 16 dispatch says the enemy was reinforced by infantry during the night of the 11th, and his report says the enemy's cavalry was superior in numbers during the period.
claims.rationale: No counts for the engaged forces; the accounts conflict on relative numbers and on Confederate infantry. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory; NPS says it prevented Sheridan from reaching Charlottesville and joining Hunter. Sheridan called the engagement of the 12th the most brilliant of the campaign but says Torbert's fighting made the Mallory's Ford route impossible without another battle; Hampton says the enemy fell back in confusion and that Sheridan was defeated at Trevilian.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,600 total; the live field reads 2,078 (US 1,007; CS 1,071). Sheridan's June 16 dispatch gives about 575 killed and wounded (490 wounded) and not over 160 captured, with 20 officers and 500 men taken on the 11th. Hampton gives his own division's loss as 59 killed, 258 wounded and 295 missing (612), and says 570 prisoners were taken and about 125 Union wounded left behind.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Hampton's figure is for his own division only; Fitzhugh Lee's losses are not given.

open_questions: Torbert's, Gregg's, Custer's and Fitzhugh Lee's reports, the revised return for Sheridan's second expedition (p.186) and Humphreys' Chapter VIII remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
